title: Two weeks, sixty hours, one cloud badge

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if studying for a cloud exam felt a bit like playing a video game? That's roughly how Antoine passed the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner in about two weeks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two weeks? That's quick. How many hours are we talking about?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: About sixty. The trick was mixing formats so he never got bored. Think of it like a workout plan: one day weights, one day cardio, so you keep showing up.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So what was in the mix?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Week one was a Udemy video course with hands-on labs, to build the vocabulary. Week two was the fun part: AWS Cloud Quest, then the Escape Room, practice exams and an exam prep course on AWS Skill Builder.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cloud Quest sounds like a game.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It is. It's a role-playing course where you solve quests that teach the same AWS services. Antoine says it was easier to finish a quest on a tired evening than another lecture chapter, and the quests map to real cloud decisions.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Timed, exam-style challenges. You reason through scenarios instead of reciting definitions, and you get used to the format and the clock before the real thing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He booked through Pearson VUE, which offers in-person or online proctoring. Here's a handy tip: if English isn't your first language, AWS offers an accommodation called ESL plus thirty, which adds thirty minutes. You request it in your AWS Certification account before you schedule.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good to know. Anything for people taking it online?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Log in at least thirty minutes early, keep the room clean, test the proctoring software the day before, and tell the household so nobody knocks mid-question.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A digital badge arrives through Credly two or three days later. You accept it with the same email as your AWS account and share it on LinkedIn or your résumé.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the takeaway is: mix formats, make it playful, book while it's fresh.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. The full write-up has screenshots of every step if you want to copy the plan.
